newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria must not botch Creditanstalt sale - Klima.
newsitem.headline: Austria must not botch Creditanstalt sale - Klima.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Thursday the country should not behave like a "banana republic" in the six-year long privatisation saga of Creditanstalt, Austria's flagship bank.
"We must not act like a banana republic," the minister told parliament in a question-and-answer session, Austrian news agency APA reported.

Klima added he would make sure the latest tender for the government's 70 percent voting stake in the bank, which closes on November 15, would be as transparent as possible. "That is important for Austria's reputation," he said.
The minister reiterated earlier hints that he expected more than one offer for the bank to land on his desk when the deadline expires, but declined to be more specific.
A host of suitors has come and gone in the seemingly endless stop-and-go sale of the bank since it was first put on the government's privatisation list in 1991.

Several international bidders have dropped their interest after they felt they were discriminated against during the due diligence process because of anti-foreign leanings in the country's top business and political circles.
Klima has said he expects the sale of the government's 19.9 million shares in the bank to be wrapped up before year-end. At current market value, the stake is worth about 14 billion schillings.
